explanation: Lye, a strong alkali, speeds up browning on the dough's surface. It is caustic, but baking turns it into harmless compounds, leaving the dark, chewy skin.

claims.text: Traditional German pretzels (Laugenbrezeln) are dipped in a lye solution before baking.
German pretzels are not dipped in sugar syrup, black tea or vinegar to make their crust.
The alkaline lye speeds the browning (Maillard) reactions on the pretzel's surface.
Lye is caustic, but during baking it reacts with carbon dioxide and becomes harmless.
